doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Storyville record in Boston
summary: Konitz thinks he sounds nervous on the Storyville record, from playing too many notes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Not long after you got off the band . . . I have a recording of yours that you did at Storyville up in Boston with Ronnie Ball and Percy Heath and Al Levitt. That’s one of my favorites of your records from the early fifties. There’s just something about the playing and how it’s recorded. Do you remember that?

I do, yeah. I’m kind of disturbed with some of my playing on that record. It sounds pretty nervous to me. I was smoking and doing things like that with the idea of not sounding so nervous but there it was.
Could’ve fooled me, put it that way.

It all has to do with using too many notes and not giving each note enough time to resolve. Just feeling the need through the influences I had all around me to play without taking a breath almost. I’m thankful that I can take a breath now and dig in a little deeper on the notes.
